security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown fences, official resource links, or local diagnostic steps, not hidden execution or exfiltration. I confirmed the cache deletion commands and force-kill command substitution as medium operational risks because the skill allows Bash. No prompt injection or malicious intent evidence was found.

remediation.suggestion: Add explicit user confirmation before deleting Metro or Haste cache directories under /tmp, and explain the expected files first.
Prefer a graceful process stop, or ask the user to confirm the PID before running a kill -9 command on port 8081.
Tell agents to inspect errors and explain command effects before simulator resets, dependency reinstalls, global installs, or build cleans.

content.value_statement: Mobile app debugging often stalls when logs, caches, native builds, and platform tools are mixed together. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a focused React Native and Expo troubleshooting workflow.
actual_capabilities: Troubleshoots Metro cache, dependency, and module resolution issues.
Guides iOS pod resets, Android Gradle cleans, and Expo prebuild cleanup.
Lists commands for Metro logs, iOS logs, Android logs, and ADB checks.
Provides a checklist for reproduction, recent changes, errors, dependencies, and platform scope.
Shows basic performance timing and memory cleanup patterns.
Links to React Native, Expo, and Flipper debugging resources.
limitations: Requires user-provided error logs, platform details, and recent change context.
Some commands can modify local files, caches, simulators, devices, or processes.
Focuses on React Native and Expo, not all native mobile applications.
Does not replace current vendor documentation or project-specific release procedures.

use_cases.title: Resolve Metro Startup Failures
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to isolate cache, dependency, import, and package compatibility problems before clearing state.

use_cases.title: Collect Mobile Crash Evidence
use_cases.description: Gather platform logs, reproduction steps, recent changes, and environment details before assigning a crash fix.

use_cases.title: Prepare Build Failure Triage
use_cases.description: Separate Expo, iOS pod, Android Gradle, and native module causes during release troubleshooting.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Metro Error
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner troubleshooting for local startup failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: I am seeing a Metro bundler error in a React Native or Expo app. Ask for the key error text, recent changes, package manager, platform, and project type. Then suggest safe first checks before any cleanup commands.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Native Build Failure
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate triage for iOS or Android build errors.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me investigate an iOS or Android native build failure. Separate likely dependency, pod, Gradle, and native module causes. Explain which logs to collect before recommending clean or rebuild commands.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a Performance Problem
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced debugging for slow screens or memory symptoms.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React Native screen performance issue. Identify likely slow renders, memory leaks, and logging points. Prioritize changes that do not alter app behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Crash Debug Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced incident planning for production mobile failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a structured debugging plan for a production mobile crash. Include reproduction steps, log sources, platform differences, dependency checks, and risk notes before any destructive command.

output_examples.input: An Expo app reports an unresolved module after package updates.
output: Checks recent dependency changes and import paths.
Suggests reading the full Metro stack trace and verifying package compatibility.
Recommends cache cleanup only after simpler checks fail.

output_examples.input: Android build fails after adding a native module.
output_examples.output: Separates Gradle, SDK, and module compatibility checks. It asks for Logcat or build output and recommends a clean rebuild only after evidence supports it.

output_examples.input: A screen feels slow while scrolling.
output: Points to render timing, expensive state updates, and memory cleanup.
Suggests measuring affected components before changing architecture.
Calls out platform differences between iOS and Android.

best_practices: Share exact error text, platform, project type, and recent changes before asking for command suggestions.
Review every shell command before execution, especially cleanup, reinstall, simulator reset, and process kill steps.
Keep a clean reproduction path and compare iOS and Android behavior separately.
anti_patterns: Do not run destructive cache or simulator reset commands before saving work and checking the error.
Do not mix multiple cleanup steps in one attempt when you need to identify the root cause.
Do not ignore native logs when JavaScript stack traces are incomplete.

faq.question: Can this skill run debugging commands?
faq.answer: It can guide tools that support Bash, but users should approve commands that modify files, caches, devices, or processes.

faq.question: Does it support Expo and bare React Native?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Expo, Metro, native modules, iOS pods, Android Gradle, and device logs at a high level.

faq.question: Can it fix crashes automatically?
faq.answer: No. It helps collect context and choose steps, but code changes and native fixes still require user review.

faq.question: Is it safe for production apps?
faq.answer: Use it for investigation and planning. Avoid cleanup or reset commands against production environments without a backup.

faq.question: Does it replace React Native documentation?
faq.answer: No. It includes documentation links and should be used with current project-specific and vendor guidance.

faq.question: Which AI tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
